source.title: a1: Steep Test-time Scaling Law via Environment Augmented Generation
source.authors: Lingrui Mei; Shenghua Liu; Yiwei Wang; Baolong Bi; Yuyao Ge; Jun Wan; Yurong Wu; Xueqi Cheng

record.tranche_reason: Reports performance as inference-time thinking-token budgets increase, extending scaling analysis to test-time reasoning rather than held-out pretraining loss or training compute.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-time reasoning accuracy curves in Figure 6. It does not report held-out cross-entropy losses or fit pretraining power laws. Table 3 and the ablations compare benchmark performance but do not vary scale, so they are not rows for these versions.
record.test_reason: The 'scaling law' in the title is test-time scaling: accuracy of one fine-tuned 32B model (a1) against the s1 baseline as the inference thinking-token budget grows. No model size, pretraining tokens, training compute or pretraining loss is varied. V6 is about downstream gains with model/pretraining scale or loss, which this study does not vary, so no version is tested. Figure 2 plots fine-tuning example counts across different models, a cross-model comparison rather than a scale sweep.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors claim a 'steep test-time scaling' pattern: environment interaction costs tokens early, then pays off at larger inference budgets, with advantages growing with task complexity. The evidence is a single-model comparison against s1 in Figure 6, with no fitted law and little numerical detail.
record.recipe_differences: This study varies inference-time thinking-token budgets and measures reasoning-benchmark accuracy; it does not fit pretraining-loss power laws or optimize training compute allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported advantage varies with inference-time token budget and benchmark; on MATH500 the model may lag at 512-2K tokens, with an inflection around 4K-8K.

fits_no_version.finding: a1-32B lags s1 at low thinking budgets (512-2K on MATH500), then overtakes it after an inflection around 4K-8K tokens. The advantage reaches 15 pp on AIME24 at 32K tokens and holds on GPQA Diamond beyond 4K.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test-time scaling: reasoning accuracy rises with the inference thinking-token budget, and tool-feedback-augmented models show steeper scaling than plain long-CoT models.

record.problems: Figure 6 provides the curves, but the text gives few numerical values beyond the 15 pp AIME24 advantage at 32K tokens; uncertainty estimates are not stated. The results concern test-time reasoning accuracy, not pretraining loss scaling.

untested.parts: All: no pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
All: no extrapolation of fitted laws.
All: no shape variation at fixed parameter count.
All: no power-law fits in other regimes. Fine-tuning data size is not swept for a single model.
Downstream performance versus model or pretraining scale or loss. Only the inference token budget is varied, for one model size.

record.verdict_notes: The title uses 'scaling law', but no law is fitted and no training scale is varied. The record's V6 link and labels should be dropped. The appendix theory sections are duplicated and have no bearing on the claim.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, training tokens, or training compute.
Extrapolation of power-law fits from smaller training runs to larger runs.
Compute-optimal allocation between model parameters and training tokens.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
Tests performance against inference-time thinking-token budgets on reasoning benchmarks; does not test predictability from pretraining loss or model-size/training-scale laws.
Dependence of pretraining-loss exponents or compute-optimal allocations on fit choices or setup.
